newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures slip on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures slip on profit taking.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures reversed early gains to end lower across the board on Wednesday, as the yen"s rise against the dollar fuelled profit taking after the three distant months hit life-of-contract highs, traders said.
Prices ranged from 90 yen to 480 yen per tonne lower. The most-active contract, benchmark March, was off 180 yen at 16,320 yen. Daily volume was estimated at 188,977 lots.
Prices opened firmer, following gains in the Chicago overnight market.
"Buying interest here ebbed later, as fundamentals in the Chicago market remained bearish," one trader said.
The May corn futures contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system was quoted at $2.82 per bushel, compared with $2.82-3/4 on the previous trading day.
The March soybean contract on the overnight trading system was quoted at $7.79 per bushel, flat from the previous trading day.
